episodes.171602: Monsoon moisture increased across the Four Corners region as a shortwave disturbance lifted overhead. This led to an uptick in shower and thunderstorm activity. Storms were slow moving and produced heavy rain which led to localized debris flows in portions of Mesa and Ouray counties. Additionally, moderate instability led to some stronger thunderstorms; one of which produced a funnel cloud in Dolores County.
episodes.171755: A rather strong cold front approached Vermont, during the afternoon and evening hours of August 26th in a marginally unstable air mass. A few thunderstorms developed in New York and moved into western Vermont. One such storm during the evening hours produced a very small, brief but intense microburst in Clarendon that destroyed a barn and a dozen or so trees.  Five people were trapped, then rescued with minor injuries but 75 cattle (cows) were trapped with 50 needing to be euthanized.
episodes.171894: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters around Tampa Bay.
episodes.172242: This periods began with a departing wave, but still under the influence of the moisture field. At the same time, another weak tropical wave approaches from the east, resulting in enough low level moisture and convergence that, when combined with local effects, generated numerous afternoon showers and thunderstorms.
episodes.172258: A severe thunderstorm developed over northeastern Campbell County and tracked east into Crook County. The storm produced large hail in the Oshoto area.
episodes.172259: A severe thunderstorm tracked east from Wyoming across the northern Black Hills area and Meade County. The storm produced hail and wind gusts as high as 80 mph.
episodes.172264: Thunderstorms became severe as they moved east of the Black Hills across the west central South Dakota plains. They formed into a line as they moved toward central South Dakota, with wind gusts over 60 mph observed across parts of the area.
episodes.172278: A couple of isolated thunderstorms produced some severe wind gusts across Stillwater and Yellowstone Counties.
episodes.172305: A storm downed a tree in Red Oak. The AWOS recorded a peak wind gust of 55 mph.
episodes.172608: Surface trough was situated along the northeast Florida coast. Aloft, ridging stretched from Bermuda southwestward across the Florida peninsula as troughing built over the southeastern states. This weather pattern created a loose surface pressure pattern across our area with deep west-southwesterly flow maintaining the anomalously moist airmass over the area, with PWATs near 2.2 inches. The sea breezes developed and shifted inland in the afternoon and eventually merged along the I-75 corridor in the evening. Around 4 inches of rain fell in Marion county near Lake Weir. A couple of storms back built into the Atlantic developing waterspouts off the Flagler county coast.
episodes.172610: Surface trough was situated along the northeast Florida coast. Aloft, ridging stretched from Bermuda southwestward across the Florida peninsula as troughing built over the southeastern states. This weather pattern created a loose surface pressure pattern across our area with deep west-southwesterly flow maintaining the anomalously moist airmass over the area, with PWATs near 2.2 inches. The sea breezes developed and shifted inland in the afternoon and eventually merged along the I-75 corridor in the evening. Around 4 inches of rain fell in Marion county near Lake Weir. A couple of storms back built into the Atlantic developing waterspouts off the Flagler county coast.
episodes.172785: A decaying storm produced an isolated severe wind gust in Lamar, CO.
episodes.173473: A typical summertime pattern prevailed with scattered afternoon thunderstorms across the tri-state region. A few storms produced heavy rain with localized flooding.
episodes.173511: A shortwave trough lifted out of the central plains and into Iowa in the afternoon. Scattered convection on the leading edge of the trough produced a couple damaging wind gusts and hail thanks to moderate instability around 1500 J/kg and dry low levels. As the column saturated the instability diminished and reduced the threat for severe storms but increasing the rainfall efficiency as the system congealed into a mesoscale convective system overnight. A widespread two to three inches of rain fell across the area. No flash flooding was reported and while appreciated, the rain did little to reduce the expanding drought impacts.
episodes.173670: A cluster of thunderstorms developed near the Blue Ridge and moved southeast into the Piedmont during the evening. Brief damaging wind gusts occurred in Franklin County.
episodes.173737: Seasonably high moisture levels led to the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms over the SE Florida coastal waters, with one spawning a waterspout.
episodes.173759: Thunderstorms moved through eastern Montana and approached western North Dakota where an unstable environment with elevated deep layer shear was present. One storm became severe, producing half-dollar size hail at Beach in Golden Valley County.
episodes.173807: Monsoon moisture fueled scattered thunderstorms over southeast California. Many storms produced flash flooding, and a few produced severe weather.
episodes.173813: High pressure situated south of the International Border led to a westerly flow aloft, which caused dry air advection. However, there was still sufficient moisture (PWAT around 1.5 inches) and instability (MLCAPE 1000-2000 J/KG) as well as a subtle disturbance in the upper-levels to result in the development of strong thunderstorms across portions of south-central and southwest Arizona. Downdraft CAPE values were also in excess of 1500 J/KG, which led to favorable conditions for some of these thunderstorms to produce severe wind gusts.
episodes.173834: Nearly stationary storms formed along a stationary front across southeast Virginia, resulting in heavy rain and flash flooding on August 27.
episodes.173862: A thunderstorm produced flash flooding in a canyon in Zion National Park.
episodes.173868: Thunderstorms in Tooele County brought strong outflow winds.
episodes.173882: With the approach of a strong mid-level wave, a cluster of multicellular storms evolved within a weakly unstable and weakly-sheared environment.  A fair amount of dry air at lower levels made for 600 J/kg or more of DCAPE, with storms producing some spotty significant wind damage along a track from near Paullina to around Primghar.
episodes.174024: Low level moisture was plentiful across northern Arizona with surface dewpoints in the 50s to low 60s. Instability was highest along/south of the Mogollon Rim, with mean MUCAPE from HREF at 1000-1500 J/kg in Yavapai County in the afternoon. General storm motion toward was to the east at 10-15 MPH with light low level flow.

A Flood Control District of Maricopa County Stream Gauge of Jackrabbit Wash at Vulture Mine Road reported water levels rising rapidly above alarm stage at around 1713 MST, with a peak flow of 4.88 feet (3651 cfs) at 1803 MST, and going back down below alarm stage at around 1926 MST. This amount of water flow likely flooded Aguila Road upstream of the gauge and Wickenburg Road, where a water rescue was performed, located 5 miles downstream of the gauge. No injuries were reported. Based on the report from the Phoenix Dispatch, water got halfway up on an unoccupied vehicle stuck along the flood waters from Jackrabbit Wash located along Wickenburg Road.
